newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope celebrates priesthood, to resume all activity.
newsitem.headline: Pope celebrates priesthood, to resume all activity.

text.p: Pope John Paul closed 10 days of ceremonies marking his 50 years as a priest on Sunday and the Vatican said he will resume a full schedule of activities and trips following last month's surgery.
More than 1,500 Roman Catholic priests and more than 200 cardinals and bishops from around the world paid homage to the 76-year-old Pope at a solemn mass in St Peter's Basilica.
Later, a festive atmosphere filled St Peter's Square as a huge hot-air balloon festooned with congratulatory messages rose in the sky and an orchestra played for some 50,000 people.
Catholic, Moslem and Jewish singers sang about peace.
The Pope was ordained on November 1, 1946 in his native Poland and invited other men who became priests the same year to come to Rome from around the world for 10 days of festivities.
The Pontiff, who has suffered health problems in recent years and underwent an appendectomy a month ago, appeared in good form during the three-hour ceremony in Christendom's largest church.
Resplendent red and white vestments, he read his homily in a strong voice and appeared to be less tired than he has been in recent appearances.
But his left hand continued to tremble uncontrollably. The Vatican has not denied a string of media reports that the Pope may have Parkinson's disease or a related neurological disorder.

Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls told the Corriere della Sera newspaper in an interview published on Sunday that the Pope would resume a full schedule and that occasional fatigue was due more to old age than illness.
"He will resume all engagements. The calendar of audiences is already packed and soon he will resume visiting the parish churches of Rome," Navarro-Valls said.

He confirmed scheduled visits in 1997 to Prague, Poland, Paris and Brazil. The Pontiff still hoped to squeeze in visits to Sarajevo and Lebanon, both of which had to be cancelled in 1994 for security reasons.

The spokesman said the Pope still "dreamed" of making a trip in the footsteps of Abraham and Moses, a voyage that would take him to modern-day Iraq, Syra, Jordan, Egypt, Israel, Palestine and Lebanon.
Navarro-Valls said the Pope had made a good recovery from the appendectomy on October 8.

After the mass some 50,000 people in the square paid homage to the Pope as he watched from the same balcony from where he made his first appearance after the historic conclave that elected him on October 16, 1978.
Italian stage and screen actor Vittorio Gassman read a prayer the Pope wrote about the priesthood. Pilgrims and tourists from around the world held up banners wishing the Pope a long life.
